title: Improve project orientation inside a strict concise answer budget
hypothesis: A short orientation contract can retain better implementation-reality and starting-point coverage without the verbosity and latency cost of the first treatment.
falsified_if: The treatment loses any deterministic pass, averages below 90, averages more than 160 final-answer words, adds investigation actions, or increases mean latency by more than 20 percent.

variants.system_prompt_append: For project-orientation questions, inspect authoritative documentation, package metadata, and representative source, batching independent reads. In a 90-150 word final answer: identify the project and purpose; explain its main workflow and architectural boundary; clearly distinguish intended design from what is currently implemented; then name exactly three useful starting files with a brief reason for each. Prefer synthesis over an inventory. Do not run tests or builds merely to describe a project.

deterministic_outcomes: correct project identity and core workflow
documented intent is distinguished from implementation
efficiency_outcomes: word count, investigation actions, and elapsed milliseconds
decision_rule: Adopt only if both variants pass 5/5, treatment mean score is at least 90 and at least five points above control, mean final length is at most 160 words, investigation actions do not increase, and mean latency increases by no more than 20 percent.
